text: Maedoc was an Irish legendary figure. He is also called Mogue, Maodhóg, or Saint Maedoc. Some early Christian saints of Ireland hold traits that seem tied to the Celtic Otherworld. Maedoc is one of them. He is linked to Leinster, the eastern province of Ireland. He was said to have been born after a double portent. His mother, queen Eithne, saw the moon enter her husband's mouth. At that very moment her husband saw a star enter hers. Eithne is also the name of a goddess. In 598 C.E. Maedoc set out on the back of a sea monster from Wales. There he had given the last rites to the land's patron saint, David. In Ireland Maedoc quickly converted the local chieftain and built a church. He eventually became bishop of Ferns, then the capital of the province.
